1.w: These also [are] proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied down:

2.w: The glory of God [is] to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings [is] to search out a matter.

3.w: The heavens for height and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings cannot be searched.

4.w: Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel will come forth for the refiner.

5.w: Remove the wicked before the face of the king, and his throne will be established in righteousness.

6.w: You should not exalt yourself before the face of the king, and in the place of the great ones you should not stand.

7.w: For better that he says to you “Come up here!” Than to set you low before a noble. That which your eyes have seen,

8.w: you should not go out to dispute hastily, for what will you do in the end when your neighbor has put you to shame?

9.w: Dispute your cause with your neighbor, and do not uncover the secret to another,

10.w: lest the one hearing [it] should bring shame to you, and your defamation shall not turn back.

11.w: Apples of gold in figures of silver, [is] a word spoken at its right time.

12.w: A ring of gold and an ornament of fine gold, [is] a wise one giving rebuke to a listening ear.

13.w: Like the cold of snow in time of harvest, [is] a faithful messenger to those sending him, and he restores the soul of his lords.

14.w: Clouds and wind and no rain, [is] a man boasting in gifts of deception.

15.w: With slowness of anger a ruler may be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.

16.w: You have found honey, eat your sufficiency, lest you be filled up with it and vomit it out.

17.w: Make rare your foot from the house of your neighbor, lest he have his fill of you and hate you.

18.w: A club or a sharpened sword, or an arrow, [is] a man answering against his neighbor a testimony of falsehood.

19.w: A tooth broken or a foot tottering [is] trust in one acting treacherously in a day of distress.

20.w: One taking away a garment in a day of cold, [or] vinegar on soda, [is] one singing with songs to a heart of misery.

21.w: If your enemy [is] hungry, give him bread, and if [he is] thirsty, give him water to drink,

22.w: For [in so doing] you will be heaping burning coals upon his head, and YHWH will give recompense to you.

23.w: A north wind twists out rain, and a secret tongue [brings] faces of indignanation.

24.w: Better to sit on the corner of roof, than with a wife of quarrels and a house of company.

25.w: Cold water over a weary soul, [is] good news from a land far away.

26.w: A spring made foul or a well spoiled [is] a righteous one swaying before the face of a wicked one.

27.w: To eat much honey [is] not good, [nor] the searching for his own honor.

28.w: A city breached, without a wall, [is] a man who [is] without restraint to his spirit.
